note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Painful, cracked, itchy dry skin on both palms for 3–4 months; worsening with significant pain and fissuring; interferes with work; occasional bleeding only after scratching. Works as a hotel housekeeper with frequent exposure to cleaning chemicals and inconsistent glove use. History of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Relevant family medical history:  Diabetes; no known skin disease, asthma, or inflammatory bowel disease.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). OTC emollient “E45” tried—no benefit. Oral antihistamine tried—no benefit.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Not recorded; patient reports generally “doesn’t hydrate very much.”
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Non-smoker. Alcohol: a couple of pints per week (minimal).
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Works as a hotel housekeeper; recently changed jobs; has taken 3 days off work due to hand symptoms. Caring responsibilities not recorded.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Subacute–chronic painful, fissured, itchy palmar dermatitis temporally associated with new hotel housekeeping role and repeated exposure to cleaning agents; inconsistent glove use. No systemic symptoms. Type 2 diabetes may contribute to xerosis and impaired skin barrier/repair. OTC emollient and antihistamine ineffective.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx and transcript):
  - Irritant contact hand dermatitis due to wet work/cleaning chemicals (High likelihood): Strong temporal link to new job, chemical exposure, and glove nonuse; symptoms on palms with fissuring and pain.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis to occupational agents (Moderate likelihood): Possible sensitization to cleaning product components or glove chemicals; may coexist with irritant dermatitis.
  - Asteatotic/xerotic eczema, diabetes-related (Moderate likelihood): Baseline generalized dryness and diabetes may exacerbate hand fissuring.
- Working diagnosis: Occupational irritant contact dermatitis of the hands with xerosis; diabetes mellitus type 2 (existing).
- Management priorities: Reduce exposure to irritants, restore skin barrier, control inflammation, and reassess response.

Management Plan

- Treatments and recommendations provided:
  - Wear protective gloves consistently during all cleaning tasks; avoid direct contact with cleaning chemicals.
  - Topical corticosteroid prescribed for inflamed areas (potency/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Stronger emollients advised liberally 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
  - Prescription sent to pharmacy.
- Follow-up:
  - Reassess in 10–14 days; return earlier if spreading, worsening, or not improving.
- Patient education:
  - Discussed likely diagnosis (dermatitis/contact dermatitis), role of irritants, and importance of barrier protection and regular emollient use.
- Rationale: DDx supports irritant contact dermatitis as most likely given occupational exposure and pattern; allergic contact dermatitis and xerosis remain considerations if inadequate response.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Irritant contact hand dermatitis (High): Onset after job change; frequent exposure to detergents/disinfectants; inconsistent glove use; palmar fissuring, pain, and itch typical.
- Allergic contact dermatitis to occupational agents (Moderate): Potential sensitization to cleaning product components or glove chemicals; pruritic chronic hand dermatitis could reflect mixed allergic/irritant etiology.
- Asteatotic/xerotic eczema, diabetes-related (Moderate): Baseline dry skin and diabetes contribute to barrier dysfunction and fissuring; occupational wet work likely exacerbates.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), anthropometrics (height/weight/BMI/waist), immunization review, oral/ear/vision exams, urinalysis, diabetes monitoring (HbA1c, lipids, foot exam), sexual and reproductive history, STI screening, mental health screening, hearing/vision concerns, detailed medication dosing, and preventive care planning.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Some audio gaps/unclear segments (e.g., alcohol quantity phrasing, product names), but core history and plan are understandable.
